title: Resilience Interlock: Cross-team SLO & Rollout Project Plan
content:
Summary:

This document captures a practical, cross-functional project plan to roll out a repeatable SLO program across a set of pilot services and then scale organization-wide. The emphasis is on fast feedback, clear owner-level accountability, and low-friction instrumentation so product, platform, and SRE can evaluate cost vs. reliability trade-offs.

Why now:
- Multiple teams have ad-hoc SLIs but inconsistent definitions and no shared reporting; makes incident prioritization and investment decisions hard.
- Upcoming Dedicated customer onboarding requires predictable latency and availability contracts.
- We need a repeatable playbook that ties SLO changes to rollout, alerts, and runbooks.

Primary objectives (measurable):
- Define and publish baseline SLO templates for 3 pilot service archetypes (API-frontdoor, async-worker, embedding-store) by 2025-02-14.
- Instrument SLIs for the pilots and ship dashboards within 4 weeks of instrumentation completion.
- Achieve production-quality alerts and one validated incident runbook per pilot within the pilot period.
- Produce a decision memo (cost vs. latency tradeoffs) and recommended rollout path for the rest of the org by 2025-04-01.

Scope (in):
- Three pilot services (names below).
- SLI definitions for latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate (4xx/5xx), and availability (successful request ratio).
- Dashboards in the Redwood Console and Grafana links.
- Runbooks and alert thresholds aligned to burn-rate rules.

Scope (out):
- Deep infra refactors (e.g., re-architecting serving runtime) — those will be follow-on projects.
- Customer contract negotiations — we provide operational posture input only.

Pilot service candidates and rationale:
- service-auth (API-frontdoor): high request rate, latency sensitive, easy to instrument
- embeddings-store (async-worker + datastore): IO-bound, good test of availability and backpressure SLIs
- completion-proxy (edge-routing to model clusters): critical for customer latency SLAs, useful for testing fallback policies

Stakeholders and RACI (high-level):
- Product Manager (PM): Maya Thompson — R (requirements, acceptance)
- SRE Lead: Jordan Lee — A (overall plan, runbook validation)
- Platform/Infra Eng: Ravi Patel — C (instrumentation ownership, metrics plumbing)
- Service Owners: Sofia Alvarez, Kenji Watanabe — R (service-level changes, deployment)
- Observability: Priya Natarajan — C (dashboards, alert routing)
- Solutions Eng / SE: Claire Huang — I (customer impact and messaging)

Milestones & timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (2025-01-08): Kickoff + alignment workshop (attendees: PMs, SRE, Platform, Service Owners)
- Week 1 (2025-01-13): SLO template v0 published for review (three archetypes)
- Weeks 2–3 (2025-01-20 to 2025-01-31): Instrumentation sprint (metrics tags, metrics ingestion, metrics schemas)
- Week 4 (2025-02-07): Dashboards + alerts smoke test
- Week 6 (2025-02-21): Pilot validation: incident runbook tested via tabletop exercise
- Week 10 (2025-03-21): Cost/latency analysis and decision memo draft
- Week 16 (2025-04-25): Org rollout plan approved / handoff to platform enablement

Deliverables per pilot:
- SLO doc (template filled for the service) with owner signoff
- Instrumentation checklist (metrics names, tags, aggregation windows)
- Grafana + Console dashboards links
- Alert config (pager, slack, severity mapping) and burn-rate mapping
- Runbook and post-incident review (PIR) template

SLO template (example fields to capture):
- SLO name: e.g., Completion API availability
- SLI definition: numerator / denominator (e.g., successful_complete_requests / total_requests)
- Window: rolling 30d and 7d
- Target: 99.9% (30d), 99.5% (7d) — specific values vary by archetype
- Error budget: 0.1% (30d)
- Alerting thresholds: burn-rate and short-window degradation alarms

Instrumentations notes (operational guidance):
- Prefer library-based metrics emission (common client wrapper) so tag conventions are consistent (service, environment, route_id, model_variant)
- Use aggregated counters + histograms for latency (expose p50/p95/p99 via downstream metrics pipeline)
- Ensure 1:1 mapping between metric name used in SLO and dashboard panels (avoid aliasing)

Alerting and burn-rate policy (proposal):
- Two-tier alerts: 1) short-window degradation notice to service owner and oncall (non-pager, slack) at 5x short-window burn rate; 2) pager at sustained >10x burn rate or crossing 7d target threshold
- Escalation matrix documented in runbook; SRE review required if burn rate exceeds threshold for >3 hours

Risk register (top items):
- Missing metrics for legacy components — mitigation: lightweight proxy instrumentation and temporary synthetic checks
- Noise from poorly aggregated metrics — mitigation: require rollup guidance in instrumentation checklist
- Org bandwidth — mitigation: phased rollout and limited pilots with tight owner accountability

Dependencies:
- Metrics pipeline team (ingestion and storage quotas)
- Redwood Console dashboards team (templating for SLO pages)
- Release engineering window for pilot services (coordination with release-engineering)

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30-min sync during pilot phase (Mon 09:30 PST) — status + blockers
- Bi-weekly stakeholder digest (email + short Confluence update)
- Dedicated Slack channel: #sre-resilience-interlock (purpose: quick triage, links to dashboards and incident notes)

Success criteria (how we know the pilot worked):
- All three pilots have production SLO pages and runbooks published with owner signoff
- At least one real incident handled with the new runbook and a completed PIR within 7 days
- Dashboards show stable measurement (no missing data) and alerts have <20% false-positive rate during pilot period

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Finalize exact p99 target buckets for completion-proxy (cost-latency tradeoffs)
- Decide whether synthetic checks count toward primary availability SLI for embeddings-store
- Determine retention window for SLO dashboards in Redwood Console (30d vs 90d)

Immediate next steps (owner tags):
- Jordan Lee: schedule kickoff and prep SLO template v0 (due 2025-01-10)
- Ravi Patel: validate instrumentation feasibility with metrics pipeline (due 2025-01-15)
- Service Owners: review v0 template and provide preliminary service specifics (due 2025-01-17)

Notes to self / working items:
- Keep templates minimal — goal is iteration velocity over completeness.
- Try to roll runbook validation into an already-scheduled oncall drill to reduce meeting overhead.
- Track effort in PROJ-312 and keep statuses brief in weekly digest.

Appendix: quick SLO archetype guidance (short):
- Latency-sensitive frontdoor: prioritize p99 and tail latency; aggressive short-window alerts
- Async worker: prioritize availability + queue depth SLIs; use synthetic workers where needed
- Edge routing/completion proxy: prioritize combined success+latency SLO; consider multi-region routing behavior

Contact: Jordan Lee (jordan.lee@redwood.example.com) — ping for questions or to volunteer a pilot service.
